cuts.raw_narration: Shinichi wakes up groggy on a green pillow and touches his own face to make sure he's real. Cut to his desk: on the turquoise surface next to his open biology textbook, what used to be his right hand is now a flesh-colored alien parasite that has split into two long stalks and is flipping the pages, studying diagrams of fish. The creature rears up into a single large eye on a stalk with a pair of human-like lips beneath it, and calmly says it is studying.

The parasite tells Shinichi it feels disappointed because it failed to occupy his brain. Shinichi recoils, sweating, and blurts out, 'You're not going to eat my brain next, are you?' The creature explains it can't now — it's already matured. It says if it had succeeded, Shinichi's head would be able to do this — and his own right hand suddenly warps in front of him into a grotesque form: a vertical mouth opens in the palm and multiple blinking eyes sprout from the fingers, all moving independently. Shinichi jerks back yelling that it's gross.

Shinichi is walking down a quiet suburban street in his brown duffle coat and green backpack. The small eye-stalk poking out of his right palm suddenly cuts him off and tells him to keep his voice down — it senses one of its own kind about 200 meters away through something like brain waves. A thin fleshy tentacle from his hand extends and points down a narrow residential street. Shinichi stares in that direction, wide-eyed.

Shinichi rounds a corner into a quiet alley and freezes. In front of him is a tri-colored dog in a little green jacket, its snout and chest smeared with fresh blood, standing over another dog it has been eating. The dog looks up at him with murderous eyes. The parasite living inside it speaks through the dog, calling Shinichi's body a poor host. Shinichi's own hand-parasite answers that it too is dissatisfied with its host, then tells him to run.

The dog-parasite lunges. Shinichi's right hand explodes outward, morphing into long whip-like tentacles tipped with eyes and blade edges. The dog-parasite mutates a pair of wings and takes to the sky, but the transformation splits its focus. A massive pale blade from Shinichi's hand swings across in mid-air, strikes the flying creature, and ruptures its core in a burst of white spray. The body drops as Shinichi stands panting in the alley.

Shinichi sits on the ground against a brick wall in a small park, breathing hard. He holds up his right hand — the parasite has shrunk back into a small fleshy shape with one eye and sharp petal-like blades still slick with dark residue. It coolly explains that its own research is the reason it won. Shinichi stares at it, hollow and bitter, and mutters that he's talking to an insect that doesn't have a shred of sympathy.
